rationale: The parent finding was established with default configuration flags. This successor runs the witness scenario under the recommended production configuration, PreVote and CheckQuorum, and with the logical clock running while the invocation is outstanding, so the held proposal cannot be attributed to default flags or to a clock that never advances. A control under the same flags shows the cluster still accepts and commits proposals from a member that was never removed.

scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API with Config.PreVote and Config.CheckQuorum both true. Node 1 campaigns and becomes leader at term 1 in configuration {1,2,3}; a remove-3 ConfChange is proposed on the leader and applied on every node; node 3 is then re-added by a committed ConfChange with leader 1 unchanged; the logical clock is advanced ten rounds with delivery between rounds; then Node.Propose is invoked on the re-added node 3 with a 1200 ms context and a 900 ms observation window, followed by a control invocation on never-removed node 2. Events record returned values, errors, elapsed times, membership, leader and payload presence.
assumptions: Ticks are delivered in ten rounds with delivery between rounds so heartbeats keep the followers' election timers reset while both timeouts advance.
CheckQuorum's activity tracking is therefore exercised (the leader keeps quorum) and PreVote's pre-election phase is available, but no election is triggered during the observation.
excluded: Message loss, partitions and leader changes
RawNode paths and async storage writes

experiment.prefix: Start nodes 1,2,3 with a MemoryStorage per node whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3} and with PreVote and CheckQuorum enabled. Node 1 campaigns at term 1 and becomes leader; every node reports leader 1 and node 1 has applied the initial entry. Propose a remove-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's own configuration excludes it; propose an add-3 ConfChange and wait until node 3 is a voter again with leader still 1. Advance the clock ten rounds with delivery between rounds and record the resulting context (leader, leader state, membership). Invoke Node.Propose on node 3 with a 1200 ms context, observe for 900 ms, and record the result and whether its payload is committed anywhere. Then invoke Node.Propose on node 2 and record its result and committed payload.
experiment.responsibility: Client-facing obligation of the Node interface under the recommended configuration: a proposal from a re-added voter with a healthy known leader must reach a decision or return an error rather than staying pending, while proposals from other members must continue to complete.

comparisons.description: Under PreVote and CheckQuorum with the clock running, the re-added voter's invocation did not return inside the window.
Its payload was not committed anywhere.
Control: the never-removed member's invocation under the same flags returned.
Control: its payload was committed on all nodes, so the group was healthy under those flags.

experiment.revision_reason: Configuration and observation change: the witness scenario now runs with Config.PreVote and Config.CheckQuorum enabled, the logical clock is advanced ten rounds with delivery between rounds before the witness invocation, and the witness and control events are emitted under their own names (checked_removal_proposed, checked_removal_applied, checked_context, checked_invocation, checked_result, checked_commit, checked_control_invocation, checked_control_result, checked_control_commit) with a 1200 ms context and a 900 ms window. The removal and re-addition are simple ConfChanges applied on every node, and four comparisons cover the pending witness invocation, its absent payload, and the control that returns and commits.
